title: Adaptive Governance Supporting an Exponentially Growing Community
guidingQuestion: How can communities govern themselves without recreating Big Tech rulebooks?
summary: Composable, adaptive governance lets communities set and evolve rules while remaining interoperable across the Meta-Layer.
humanIssue: Big Tech making all the rules
opportunity: Communities govern themselves with composable governance

hero.headline: Rules should grow with the community, not above it.
hero.text: When a handful of platforms write the terms for billions of people, local norms disappear. Adaptive governance gives communities modular tools to set policy, resolve conflict, and evolve without waiting for a corporate update.

problemStory.title: Why this matters
problemStory.scenario: A neighborhood mutual-aid group is banned overnight for a policy they never saw drafted. Appeals go into a void. The people who built the community have no say in the rules that dissolve it.

webLimitations.title: Why today's Web struggles
webLimitations.text: Platforms centralize rule-making because they own the servers, the graph, and the enforcement stack. Communities cannot take their governance with them when they leave.

futureVision.title: Imagine instead
futureVision.text: Communities compose governance modules (membership, speech norms, dispute resolution) and carry those agreements across contexts.
bullets: Governance that scales without becoming a new monopoly
